rules.problem: Type and contents right (every red-box item and every discriminating finding for a 'likely' diagnosis is listed, grouped sensibly). Trigger is broader than the page (see c001). Low impact.

rules.rule: Check for urgent lump/swelling in groin conditions
Check for mpox features in lymphadenopathy (lump in neck, axilla or groin)
rules.problem: Contents match the mpox bullet. Two softenings: the 21-day contact window is dropped (c024), and on the page this bullet sits in the 'Generalised' / 'No medication or infective cause' column, whereas the task fires on any lymphadenopathy. Broader than the page but not wrong.

rules.rule: Diagnose probable incarcerated (irreducible) inguinal hernia, lump in groin
rules.problem: Structure (groin lump AND bigger on standing/coughing/stool AND any-of [severe pain, vomiting, no stools-or-flatus 24 h, cannot be reduced]) matches the red box. 'No stools or flatus/wind' is read as neither passed (and of both), which is the literal reading; a clinician may prefer either. 'likely' -> probable is right.

rules.rule: Diagnose probable strangulated inguinal hernia, lump in groin
rules.problem: Identical evidence to the incarcerated rule, so both probable diagnoses fire together; the page does say 'incarcerated/strangulated ... likely' for the same criteria, so this is faithful.

rules.rule: Diagnose probable aneurysm, pulsating lump in groin
Diagnose probable thyroid mass, lump in neck moving on swallowing
rules.problem: 'Thyroid gland moves with swallowing' presupposes the lump is thyroid, but it is the closest SNOMED concept (no 'lump moves on swallowing' finding exists).

rules.rule: Diagnose probable inguinal hernia, lump in groin
Diagnose probable hidradenitis suppurativa, recurrent painful abscesses
rules.problem: 'painful abscesses' is encoded as site abscess AND a separate regional pain symptom (Pain in axilla / Inguinal pain / Perineal pain), which is not what the page says and makes the rule need two recorded findings per site where the page has one. Also requires 'Recurrent abscess' on top of the site abscess (double recording). The site 'or' and 'likely' -> probable are right.

rules.rule: Diagnose probable lymphadenopathy, lump in neck, axilla or groin
rules.problem: 'If none of above' is encoded as exclusion of skin lump, thyroid movement, cough impulse and recurrent abscess, which covers the non-urgent boxes but not the red box: a pulsating groin lump is not excluded, so it can be labelled probable lymphadenopathy as well as probable aneurysm. Exclusion on 'Recurrent abscess' at any site is slightly broader than the page.

rules.rule: Diagnose possible mpox in lymphadenopathy (lump in neck, axilla or groin)
rules.problem: Logic (exposure AND [rash/lesions] AND >=1 systemic) matches the bullet and 'consider mpox' -> possible is right. The 21-day window before symptom onset and 'unexplained' (rash) are dropped (c080).

rules.rule: Urgent: lump/swelling in groin with incarcerated/strangulated hernia or aneurysm
rules.problem: Urgent is justified by 'Give urgent attention' / 'Refer urgently'. Follows the house pattern (presenting complaint AND active_condition of the box's likely diagnoses). Note 'Aneurysm' is site-less, so any known aneurysm plus a groin mass would also trigger it; the page's wording is equally site-less.

summary: Nothing is invented and no number, direction or priority level is wrong; the red box, the three 'likely' boxes, lymphadenopathy and mpox are all encoded in the right rule types. The most consequential issue is the hidradenitis rule, where 'painful abscesses' is split into a site abscess plus a separate regional pain symptom (no 'Painful' qualifier exists), so the rule demands findings the page does not. Smaller imprecisions: the mpox 21-day contact window is dropped, 'Constipation' is broader than 'no stools for 24 hours', the first check task triggers on any body-region mass, and 'none of above' for lymphadenopathy does not exclude the red-box pulsating lump. Not encoded at all (outside this checker's claims but visible on the page): 'Yes: treat for bubo' for a hot, tender groin node, and the TB-aspiration trigger (cough, weight loss, night sweats or fever).
